issues.legal_issue: The market value for stamp duty on a sale deed executed pursuant to a decree of specific performance is determined when the deed is presented for registration, rather than when the prior sale agreement was made or the decree was passed.
material_facts: The buyer entered into two agreements to purchase immovable properties, but the vendor did not execute the sale deeds.
The buyer obtained decrees for specific performance and, after the vendor still failed to execute the deeds, the executing court executed them.
The buyer tendered the deeds for registration using stamp papers based on the prices in the earlier agreements.
The registering authority suspected undervaluation and referred the deeds to the Collector, who assessed their values using market values higher than the agreement prices.
The High Court directed that valuation be based on the dates the specific-performance suits were filed, taking account of the delay and the buyer’s lack of fault.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the High Court judgments were set aside. The Collector was directed to determine market value as of the dates the deeds were tendered for registration and assess the duty accordingly.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(12) and 17 of the Stamp Act, execution means signing, and a chargeable instrument must be stamped before or at execution. Read with Sections 3 and 27, the value stated in an instrument is not conclusive; Section 47-A of the Rajasthan amendment permits referral and determination of the correct market value when undervaluation is suspected. For a sale deed, the relevant market value is that at the time the deed is executed and presented for registration, not at the time of the earlier agreement or decree. A taxing statute must be construed strictly, without importing equity or hardship: A.V. Fernandez v. State of Kerala, AIR 1957 SC 657. The contrary approach in Sub-Registrar, Kodad Town and Mandal v. Amaranaini China Venkat Rao, AIR 1998 AP 252, was held to be incorrect.

predicates.court_decreed_sale_registration: A court executed a sale deed after the vendor failed to perform an agreement to sell and a decree for specific performance was obtained.
predicates.market_value_duty_instrument: The instrument concerned a transfer of immovable property for which duty was based on the property's market value.
predicates.instrument_presented_for_registration: The executed instrument was tendered to the registering authority for registration.
predicates.market_value_assessed_at_registration_pr: The property's market value is assessed as of when the executed instrument is presented for registration.

issues.definition: When a court-executed sale deed concerning immovable property is presented for registration, the rule requires its market value to be assessed at that presentation.
